ov: Five species of large tree kingfishers from Australia and New Guinea that rarely eat fish. The laughing kookaburra lives in family groups: grown offspring stay to help their parents defend the territory and raise chicks.
rg: Australia, New Guinea and the Aru Islands; the laughing kookaburra was introduced to New Zealand, Tasmania and Western Australia.
df: Lizards, insects, worms, snakes, mice and young birds.
fx: The laughing kookaburra pairs for life.
All kookaburra species are listed as least concern.
